# TSP-041 — 80 % of hourly pulses do no work: `orchestrator-pulse` checks the standing queue in bash and types the prompt only when something is queued

## Problem
`orchestrator-pulse.timer` types "Pulse: run plan-usage, then continue the standing queue … or report nothing" into the interactive `claude` session every hour it finds idle. Four weeks in, the queue is almost always empty, so the usual outcome is one full turn on a 156 k-token context that runs `plan-usage` and says nothing. The queue test it asks the model to make is three bash reads.

## Evidence
- `log/pulse.log` — 102 `fired` lines in the last 7 days (14.6/day; 20, 18, 14, 24, 23 on 10-10 → 10-14), 66 `skip` (32 "input line not empty", 26 "background agents running").
- Cross-reference of those 102 fires with `log/actions.jsonl` (interactive rows, 15 min after each fire, read-only script in this run): 82 fires produced ≤ 2 tool calls other than `plan-usage` ("no-op"), 25 produced no audit row at all; 20 led to work. `agents-log --since 4d --stats` shows `plan-usage 2>&1` = 77 rows in 4 days, one per fire.
- `agents-log --tokens --since 4d` — session `f950f2b2` (the orchestrator): 673 turns, mean context 156 182 tokens, 100.4 M cache-read tokens in 4 days. One no-op pulse is at least one turn at that size: 82 × 156 k ≈ 12.8 M cache-read tokens a week spent on "report nothing", more than ten toolsmith runs (`toolsmith/logs/index.tsv`: 1 266 755 per run).
- `KB/orchestrator.md:49-56` — the pulse procedure is already deterministic: (1) `plan-usage --check 80` exits 1 → report nothing; (2) under 80 %, first any open `pc need list` alert or failed fleet unit, then the owner-free items of the latest `HEALTH.md`; (3) nothing queued → report nothing. On 10-15 03:00: `pc need list --json` = `[]`, `systemctl --user list-units --state=failed` empty, newest `HEALTH.md` dated 2026-10-11.
- `bin/orchestrator-pulse:37-57` — the only gates today are tmux pane state (session present, no turn, no background agents, empty input line). Nothing reads the queue.

## Survey
- exists: OpenClaw's heartbeat is the same design (periodic agent turn, quiet reply `NO_REPLY`); it skips **without a model call** only when the heartbeat file is empty, gates on active hours and a busy queue, and its token note is the point: "roughly 100K tokens per run down to 2–5K" with an isolated session (https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/heartbeat, read 2026-10-15). nanobot runs a small LLM to decide whether there are active tasks (https://www.mintlify.com/HKUDS/nanobot/advanced/heartbeat, read 2026-10-15) — rejected: still a model call per tick.
- exists locally: `bin/orchestrator-pulse` (57 lines, bash), its fixture suite `bin/tests/orchestrator-pulse.test.sh` (fake `$HOME`, private tmux socket, `PULSE_LOG`), `plan-usage --check N`, `pc need list --json`, `systemctl --user list-units --state=failed --plain --no-legend`.
- rejected: an isolated pulse session (OpenClaw's 2–5 k) — the pulse exists to continue *this* session's queue with its context; an isolated turn would re-read everything. Rejected: lengthening the timer to 6 h — a real `need` alert would then wait up to 6 h; the queue check keeps the 1 h response for real items and removes only the empty turns. Rejected: a `Stop`-hook or model-side change — the saving must happen before the prompt is typed.
- chosen: queue precheck in the existing bash script, same timer, same prompt.

## Proposed change
- `bin/orchestrator-pulse`: before `send-keys`, compute `queue`: `plan-usage --check 80` (exit 1 → `skip "plan >= 80%"`); open needs = `pc need list --json | jq length`; failed units = count of `systemctl --user list-units --state=failed --plain --no-legend`; health = newest `$AGENT_WORK/research/*/*/HEALTH.md` with mtime newer than the last `fired` line in `$LOG`. If all three are zero and the last `fired` is less than `PULSE_FLOOR_H` hours old (default 6): `log skip "queue empty (needs 0, failed 0, health unchanged)"` and exit 0. Otherwise type the prompt as today, with the counts appended ("queue: needs 1, failed 0, health new") so the turn starts with the answer instead of re-deriving it. The floor keeps at most 4 unconditional pulses a day, so the session's "continue the standing queue" habit survives a quiet week.
- `bin/tests/orchestrator-pulse.test.sh`: three new cases under the existing fake `$HOME` and private tmux socket — queue empty → `skip`, one open need (stub `pc` on `PATH` printing `[{…}]`) → `fired`, floor exceeded → `fired`; `plan-usage` and `systemctl` stubbed on `PATH` so no real plan, need or unit is read. Selftest: the stub `pc` records its argv and the test fails if any stub saw a mutating verb.
- `KB/orchestrator.md` Pulse section: one sentence saying the script now does steps 1–3 and the prompt arrives with the counts.

## Success check
`metric / before (number) / target (number) / measured by (command)`

- metric: fired pulses per day; no-op fired pulses per day (≤ 2 non-`plan-usage` tool calls in the 15 min after the fire)
- before: 14.6 fired/day, 11.7 no-op/day (7 d to 10-15); work pulses 20/7 d
- target: ≤ 6 fired/day, ≤ 2 no-op/day; work pulses ≥ 15/7 d (real items still served within the hour)
- measured by: `awk -F'T' '/fired/{print $1}' ~/agents/log/pulse.log | sort | uniq -c | tail -7`; `grep -c 'skip.*queue empty' ~/agents/log/pulse.log`; the no-op cross-reference is re-run read-only by the toolsmith (fires joined to `log/actions.jsonl` interactive rows within 15 min)

## Effort
`model / sessions (integer) / resident (CPU/RSS or none)`

- model: sonnet
- sessions: 1
- resident: none (three reads per hour inside the existing timer)

## Class
auto-ok

A `bin/` script on an existing timer, no new unit; it changes how often the owner's interactive session is woken, so a `hold` row is the owner's veto if the hourly habit is wanted as is.

## Result

## Result (2026-10-17, code-review run 2026-10-17-030031)
- Files: `bin/orchestrator-pulse` (queue precheck after the idle gates: `plan-usage --check 80` exit 1 → `skip "plan >= 80%"`; needs, failed units, HEALTH.md newer than the last `fired`; all zero and last fire < `PULSE_FLOOR_H` (6) h → `skip "queue empty (…)"`; else the prompt gets ` (queue: needs N, failed N, health new|unchanged)`), `bin/tests/orchestrator-pulse.test.sh` (stubbed `pc`/`plan-usage`/`systemctl` on `PATH`, `AGENT_WORK` in the fixture; cases empty queue → skip, one need → fired, floor exceeded → fired; selftests: stubs resolve first, stubs saw only the three read-only argv), `KB/orchestrator.md` Pulse (one sentence).
- Validation: test failed first (`FAIL empty queue skips: … fired`), then 11/11 ok, rc 0; `bash -n` and `shellcheck -S warning` clean.
- Before re-read (pulse.log, 10-10 → 10-16): 20, 18, 14, 24, 23, 21, 24 fired = 144/7 d = 20.6 fired/day (the proposal's 14.6/day used a different window); `skip.*queue empty` = 0. No-op cross-reference not re-run here.
- Measurement pending on the next toolsmith run.
